title: Spectral-window kinetic corridor
question: Does a fixed low-energy spectral projection applied to the R-388 kinetic target produce a finite cutoff corridor for all sampled beta values, and does the eta=1/2 control remain unstable?

model.corridor_candidate: eta>=1 with fixed E<=4 is tested across beta=1/4,1/2,1,2
model.outside_stress: eta=1/2 is retained as a control expected to grow
model.analytic_target: Prove a cutoff-independent Gibbs tail and invariant window/core transfer before any common-alpha claim

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only positivity and the finite window-mass split; spectra, matrices, cutoff ratios and QFT limits remain Python/open analysis.

qft_interface.closed: Finite fixed-energy projected kinetic seminorms are stable over the eta=1 corridor on the declared two-site grid, while eta=1/2 is a growth control.
qft_interface.open: Uniform Gibbs-tail transfer, beta/eta independence, source/volume/shape uniformity, invariant domain, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary finite spectral-window interface only; no physical-sector conclusion or production-owner transfer is supplied.

boundary: Claim-nonbearing finite spectral-window kinetic stress only. It proves no cutoff-uniform operator or projected Gibbs estimate, no beta/eta-independent topology, no Gibbs-tail or shell summability, no domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, no OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, no gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: A finite projected corridor can guide a spectral-tail proof, but it cannot discard the complement or replace the common algebra norm without an independent uniform transfer theorem.
